    "input_encoding": "One qubit per member in the computational basis encodes x_i. Coefficients h_i and J_ij are precomputed classically from the validated, sorted preference pairs. Current assignment, score(), describe(), and gain reporting remain classical.",
    "quantum_algorithm_family": "qaoa",
    "output_decoding": "Measure the candidate bitstring, decode x_i per member, and classically recompute score() to verify the result. The contract's exactness requirement means a QAOA sample is not sufficient unless verified against the true maximum. The smallest numeric membership mask tie-break must be enforced classically, because quantum sampling has no deterministic tie ordering.",

      "Pairs are already validated, complete, unique, and sorted before quantum selection.",
      "Classical preprocessing can compute objective coefficients exactly.",
      "Exact global optimum and smallest-mask tie-breaking remain mandatory.",
      "QAOA is a heuristic proposal, not an exactness guarantee."
    ],
    "risks": [
      "QAOA may return a non-optimal assignment and thereby violate propose's exact max contract.",
      "Probabilistic sampling and parameter optimization do not preserve the deterministic smallest-mask tie-break.",
      "Objective/oracle data loading, ancilla requirements, and classical QAOA parameter optimization may outweigh the classical exhaustive loop for practical n.",
      "No workload or advantage evidence exists; quantumization could add failure modes without demonstrated benefit."
    ],
    "expected_resource_characteristics": {
      "decision_qubits": "O(n) for n members",
      "ancilla_requirements": "Undefined in this DRAFT plan; depends on pair-term phase-separation implementation",
      "classical_preprocessing": "O(M) for M=n(n-1)/2 pairs",
      "classical_verification": "O(M) per decoded candidate",
      "measurement_repetitions": "Undefined; must support finding and classically verifying an exact optimum"
    }
  },
  "rationale": "kernel.py choose at lines 12-19 is the only quantumization candidate; it exhaustively enumerates masks 0..2^n-1, builds values with member i as bit i, computes score(values,pairs), and returns the first achieved maximum in ascending numeric-mask order, thereby implementing smallest-mask tie-breaking. Activation is only in review mode == 'propose' after lines 15-31 have validated members, preferences (complete, unique, non-self, known relation), current bool vector, and sorted pairs as (i,j,w). score() is still required for current/proposed reports and verification; describe() and input validation must remain intact. Although structurally eligible, practical suitability is false: propose must maximize signed score exactly and tie-break deterministically, while QAOA is approximate and quantum sampling does not guarantee the smallest mask; no workload, hardware, encoding-cost, or advantage evidence is supplied. Therefore the correct decision is REMAIN_CLASSICAL. Benchmark support is true because the QUBO/Ising family is in the DRAFT menu. A Grover threshold-predicate search is also conceivable but requires threshold meta-search plus classical verification and tie-breaking, and does not improve practical suitability.",
  "structural_eligibility": true,
  "practical_suitability": false,
  "benchmark_supported": true,
  "computational_intent": "Exact maximum signed-score binary group assignment under complete pairwise together/apart preferences",
  "assumptions": [
    "Preference validation and all ValueError behavior remain in classical review before any selection.",
    "Pairs are complete, unique, sorted as (i,j,w), with w=+1 for apart and w=-1 for together.",
    "Groups may be empty or singleton; no capacity/group-size constraints exist.",
    "Exact global maximum and smallest numeric membership-mask tie-breaking are part of the contract.",
    "No quantum hardware, workload, encoding-cost or advantage evidence is supplied."
  ],
  "risks": [
    "QAOA/Ising sampling can violate the exact maximum semantics required by propose.",
    "Deterministic smallest-mask tie-breaking can be lost under probabilistic sampling.",
    "Quantum data loading and parameter optimization may be more expensive than the classical exhaustive search for unknown n.",
    "The shared contract menu is DRAFT; applicability does not imply validated advantage or correctness."
  ],
  "contract_applicability": [
    {
      "contract_id": "qubo-ising-v0",
      "applicable": true,
      "rationale": "The signed pair score is exactly a quadratic binary objective with no required penalty terms; coefficients can be precomputed from pairs."
    },

      "applicable": true,
      "rationale": "A finite group-assignment domain and a score >= threshold predicate can support Grover-style search as a subroutine, but finding the maximum and smallest-mask tie requires threshold meta-search plus classical verification."
    }
  ]
}
